hook: The conqueror of the Inca Empire, who could not read or write.

pages.x: Francisco Pizarro was born around 1478 in Trujillo, in Spain, the son of a soldier. He never learned to read. He sailed to the Americas in 1502, and in 1513 was with Balboa when he became the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas.

On a second expedition in 1527, stuck on a starving island off Colombia, his men wanted to go home. Pizarro drew a line in the sand with his sword: to the south lay Peru and riches, to the north Panama and poverty. Thirteen men stepped across.

In 1532, with 168 men, he met the Inca emperor Atahualpa, just victorious in a civil war, at Cajamarca. Atahualpa came with thousands of unarmed followers. When he threw down a prayer book he was handed, the Spanish opened fire with guns and cannon, charged on horseback, and took him prisoner.

Atahualpa offered to fill a room once with gold and twice with silver for his freedom. The treasure came, about six tonnes of gold, and was melted down into bars. Then Pizarro had him executed anyway.
Pizarro marched on and took the Inca capital, Cusco, in 1533. In 1535 he founded a new capital near the coast, Lima, the "City of Kings".
The conquerors fell out over the spoils. Pizarro had his partner Diego de Almagro executed, and in 1541 Almagro's followers burst into his palace in Lima and killed him.
Pizarro conquered the Inca Empire, the largest state in the Americas, with a tiny force, helped by smallpox and an Inca civil war. Peru's silver soon flowed to Europe and Asia.
pts: Opened Peru's silver to the world
